findings.claim: Every B20 member only revokes, restores or eliminates lands and 'takes effect when issued'; lead no, TERM, dated the order's own date.
findings.evidence: 49 B20 members' own held texts defer their effect to an unrecorded plat filing, e.g. EO 6943 (Jan. 9, 1935): 'is hereby revoked, this revocation to become effective upon the date of the official filing of the plats of resurvey'; EO 7272, 7244, 7153, 7392, 7454 read 'This order shall become effective upon the date of the official filing of the plat(s) of resurvey'. The 49 are EO 6760, 6846, 6943, 6977, 6980, 7066, 7131, 7132, 7133, 7147, 7153, 7175, 7218, 7227, 7240, 7244, 7264, 7269, 7271, 7272, 7275, 7279, 7280A, 7280B, 7282, 7283, 7284, 7284A, 7284B, 7290, 7326, 7327, 7328, 7335, 7344, 7355, 7360, 7362, 7374, 7376, 7392, 7434, 7454, 7506, 7507, 7511, 7527, 7528, 7529 (regex 'become effective upon the date of (the) official filing' over primary_text_path). P1 dates a spent order by 'the order's own date (or its stated effective date)'; the stated effective date here is the plat filing, which the doctrine itself says no held source gives (B29 keeps the 31 parents open for exactly that reason).
findings.fix: Add a branch before B20 that catches texts deferring effect to the plat filing ('(shall|to) become effective upon the date of (the )?(official )?filing') and leads open (kind e.g. spent_on_plat_filing_unproven, gap: plat filing date), consistent with B29; recount B20 (200) and the open total.

findings.location: B06 / verified_whole_revocations EO:3867; appendix row 'EO 3867 | B06 | EO 4653 | 1927-05-20'
findings.claim: EO 4653 revokes EO 3867 as a whole (verified by the 'revoking executive order, cited by number' test, which rejects 'as to').
findings.evidence: Held text jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4653.txt: 'Executive Order No. 3867 dated June 16, 1923, withdrawing the public lands in Ts. 5 S., Rs. 97, 98 and 99 W.; Ts. 6 S., Rs. 98 and 99 W., and Ts. 7 S., Rs. 97, 98 and 99 W. ... be and the same is hereby revoked, only as to Ts. 6 and 7 S., R. 99 W.' The qualifier follows 'revoked', so it is a partial revocation; EO 4653 is itself on B22 as a revocation with an ex-service opening.
findings.fix: Remove EO:3867 from verified_whole_revocations and from B06's list; it falls to B30/B35 open (standing resurvey withdrawal, partially revoked 1927). B06 becomes 197, revocations 221, EO revocations 89; extend the qualifier test to text after the verb.

findings.evidence: PLO_TABLE.csv and BLM text layer plo_2251-4975.txt: '4188 April 6, 1967 .. Alaska; withdrawing for administrative site revoking EO No. 5384 .... 32 FR 5837'. The appendix also gives 1967-04-06. The upper bound is ten years late.

findings.location: B20 negative conditions; members EO:4867, EO:324B, EO:5931
findings.claim: B20 members have 'no new reservation'; they are spent on issue under P1.
findings.evidence: EO 4867 (held text EO_4867.txt): EO 4758 'is, therefore, revoked and ... it is hereby ordered that the lands described below be withdrawn from settlement, entry or other disposition' (summary 'with drawn', OCR split, defeats the 'withdrawn' exclusion). EO 324B: cancels the order as to one tract 'and that the SE 1/4 of NW 1/4 of same section be withdrawn ... and reserved' (summary 'to reserve certain other lands in lieu thereof'; 'reserve' is not caught by 'reserved'). EO 5931 (ofr-compilations EO_5931.txt) Section II: 'a strip of land, 10 feet wide ... be, and the same is hereby, reserved and set apart as a right of way'. Each makes a new standing reservation, so P1 does not apply.
findings.fix: Exclude these from B20 (add 'reserve\b', 'with\s?drawn' and 'in lieu' to the exclusion, or list them) so they fall to B26/B35 open.

findings.claim: EO 576 only revokes or restores (spent on issue).
findings.evidence: Held text EO_576.txt: 'It was not intended by the exceptions contained in my several proclamations creating forest reserves ... to except from the force and effect of such proclamations lands so withdrawn; and all such lands ... will be held and considered as parts of the reserves created thereby.' It restores nothing; it is a standing construction that keeps coal-withdrawn lands inside forest reserves. It matched B20 only through 'excluded from' in the summary.
findings.fix: Remove from B20; lead open (standing order governing forest-reserve lands, possibly PD-NATIONAL-FOREST).

findings.location: B24 description and md part (c) B24 row; member EO:2641
findings.claim: B24 holds the listed amending orders, including EO 2641, each merged into the parent (P2) with the P2 disclosure.
findings.evidence: EO 2641's held text reads 'is hereby further amended by eliminating therefrom all provisions for the forfeiture of lots'; B24's text_regex ('hereby,? (?:amended|modified)|...') does not match 'hereby further amended', so EO 2641 falls to B20 and gets kind spent_on_issue with the basis 'revokes or restores lands withdrawn by another order', which is false, and without the P2 disclosure. The md lists 11 B24 names but B24 decides 10.
findings.fix: Allow 'hereby,? (?:further )?amended' in B24 (or drop the text condition for listed members) so EO 2641 lands on B24; correct the md list/count.

findings.location: B02 (EO 3529, EO 5136) vs ruling P2 and B24
findings.claim: EO 3529 and EO 5136 are yes leads because 43 CFR 2566.0-3 carries the townsite regulations as amended by them.
findings.evidence: Both orders' only content amends EO 3489's regulations (summaries: 'amended as to the collection of assessments'; 'amended to authorize the Interior Sec'y to reappraise and sell'). P2 makes such an order 'no, TERM, merged_into_parent_on_issue', and the doctrine itself gives that lead to EO 2579 and EO 2982, which amended the earlier Alaska railroad townsite regulations. P2 states that the alternative (amending order lives while the amended text lives) is an owner choice to be named in the adoption asks, not adopted inside one doctrine.
findings.fix: Give EO 3529 and 5136 the P2 lead (no, merged into EO 3489, with the disclosure and EO 3489's CURRENT predicate noted), or keep yes only as a named owner-choice ask applied consistently to B24.

findings.location: B23 basis ('Coordinator rulings P1 and 4'), B25 basis ('Coordinator ruling 4'), md B25 row ('coordinator decision 4')
findings.claim: A coordinator ruling 4 says a licence, right-of-way or permit for a continuing use lives with that use.
findings.evidence: COORDINATOR_RULINGS.md has rulings P1-P8; P4 is 'Named persons' (one act for one named person follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON). No ruling addresses continuing-use permits.

findings.location: B23, B20, B22 vs ruling P4 (named persons)
findings.claim: The doctrine decides one-act orders for named persons itself (spent_on_issue) or as land orders.
findings.evidence: P4: 'An order whose operative content is one act for one named person (appointment, reinstatement, transfer, retirement or exemption, designation to act) follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON in every family.' Members here: EO 2501 (homestead entry of Clarence E. Burr), 2551 (entry of Samuel L. Kay), 2712 (reinstatement of entries of James E. Kitchens and Van Hayes), 3178 (George W. Chapman, Assistant Secretary of the Interior, is authorized and directed to perform the duties of the Secretary') on B22, which reached B22 only because its WPA summary runs into EO 6171.

findings.claim: An earlier held revocation edge (EO 9026, 1942-01-16) 'may be partial or may be the true end', so the end lies between 1942-01-16 and 1958-09-04.

findings.location: B35 members that are executive-order Indian reservations
findings.claim: B35 standing withdrawals stay in force 'until revoked by the President (now the Secretary) or by Congress (S1, S2)'.
findings.evidence: B35 contains Indian reservation orders such as EO 1538 (Papago), 1681 (Paiute, Shoshone), 1682 (Flathead), 1772, 1903 (Goshute). Changes to executive-order Indian reservation boundaries have required an Act of Congress since Act of Mar. 3, 1927, ch. 299, sec. 4, 44 Stat. 1347 (25 U.S.C. 398d), which FLPMA sec. 704(a) touched only as to its proviso (held FLPMA p. 2792: 'Mar. 3,1927 299 4 44:1347 25 U.S.C. 398d. Only the proviso thereof.'). The B35 basis misstates who can end them, and their subject belongs to PD-INDIAN.
findings.fix: Route Indian-reservation orders to PD-INDIAN (B01_INDIAN) or give them a separate open branch with the correct basis.

findings.claim: The alternative 'modified, and the excluded lands restored' is matched.
findings.evidence: In the JSON file the alternative is written 'modified,?' + four backslash characters + 's?and the excluded lands restored' (five occurrences), which decodes to a regex with two backslashes before 's', i.e. a literal backslash followed by 's'. The alternative therefore never matches; in B20's last negative lookahead this means summaries reading 'modified, and the excluded lands restored' are excluded from B20 and fall to open branches.
findings.fix: Write the whitespace class with one JSON escape (two backslash characters in the file), as elsewhere in the doctrine.

findings.claim: The revoking order is dated only to the year, so the date is a year interval.
findings.evidence: The held revoking texts print the day: EO 4313 'September 25, 1925'; EO 4968 'September 26, 1928'; EO 2457 '20 September, 1916' (OCR).
findings.fix: Use fixed dates 1925-09-25, 1928-09-26 and 1916-09-20 (the last checked against a clean copy).

summary: The doctrine's architecture is sound and most of its evidence checks out: all 132 PLO rows in the appendix match BLM's held table for date and FR page, the 90 revoking-EO texts and dates are held and match except one, the FLPMA, Pickett Act, Midwest Oil, EO 9146/9337/10355, King Range notice, FPA and Stock-Raising Act citations are right, and the B03 BLM layer was confirmed on the web. It needs required changes before adoption. Branch B20 gives a spent-on-issue 'no' dated the order date to 49 revocations whose own texts defer their effect to an unrecorded plat filing, which contradicts ruling P1 and the doctrine's own B29 reasoning. B20 also decides four orders that make new reservations or are not restorations (EO 4867, 324B, 5931, 576) and misfiles the amending EO 2641. B06 treats EO 3867 as wholly revoked when EO 4653 revoked it 'only as to' two townships. B05_5384 dates PLO 4188 in 1977 instead of 1967. S12 cites 84 Stat. 1007 for Pub. L. 91-476, which is at 84 Stat. 1067, 1070. The Conclusions' subtotals (270, 50) and the contradiction count (62; the engine gives 48) are wrong. B23 and B25 cite a nonexistent 'coordinator ruling 4'. Named-person orders are decided here contrary to P4, B02's yes leads for two amending orders conflict with P2, and several OCR misses leave decidable members open. The open list is otherwise honest about its gaps.
